Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for Australia's reply to commence. The two umpires and players head out to the centre. Mitchell Marsh walks out to open the innings alongside Glenn Maxwell. It will be Jediah Blades to kickstart proceedings with the new ball for the home side. Blades to Marsh. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, West Indies have finished with 170 on the board, the lowest first-innings score of the series. Given how comfortably Australia have chased targets so far, the hosts do appear to be well short. That said, this is the third time this pitch at Warner Park is being used, and it does not seem to be playing as true. Shimron Hetmyer feels it’s a fighting total, but for it to become a match-winning one, West Indies will need to bowl out of their skins. Pace-off deliveries and hitting the wicket hard are likely to be the most effective options on this surface. Back in a bit for the chase.

Shimron Hetmyer of West Indies is up for a quick chat. He admits that they kept losing wickets in quick intervals, which made the difference. Highlights that he was just looking to stay at the crease and then try to build a platform for the death overs. Says he just tried to hit as straight as possible and use the wind to his advantage. Points that on a track like this, where there's not much spin on offer, it was better to take on the spinners than to react to the seamers. Mentions that he tried to get them past 200. Shares that if they pitch the ball in the right areas like the last game, and pick some early wickets, it is a good total to defend.

Shimron Hetmyer brought up his fifty even as wickets kept tumbling around him, but once he departed, the Aussies quickly closed out the innings. All six bowling options used by Mitchell Marsh chipped in with at least a wicket. Ben Dwarshuis did the early damage, removing both openers and eventually finishing with three wickets, though he was a touch expensive in the process.

Earlier, after being asked to bat first for the fifth game in a row, the hosts lost their top three inside the Powerplay. From there, the innings largely revolved around Shimron Hetmyer, who stitched together stands with Sherfane Rutherford, Jason Holder, and Matthew Forde. The tourists were quick to break stands before they could truly blossom, ensuring West Indies never quite found the momentum they were after.

A job well done by Australia! The Windies' innings followed a familiar script that has played out throughout the series. Australia kept chipping away at the wickets to stay in control, while West Indies once again saw several batters get starts without converting them into meaningful scores, apart from Shimron Hetmyer.

OUT! RUN OUT! Brilliant piece of athleticism from Nathan Ellis to wrap up the innings! He fires it very full and outside off, Jediah Blades shapes to smash it to the off side, but bumps it off the inside half of the bat. It bounces on the pitch and Hosein calls his partner through for a single. Blades rushes to the other end, obeying his partner. Nathan Ellis sprints forward towards the ball and puts in a dive before flicking the ball into the stumps at the striker's end, with Akeal Hosein struggling to make his ground. The decision is sent upstairs and the third umpire is called in action. The side-on replay shows that Akeal Hosein is out by a considerable margin and West Indies end their innings with 170 on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: In all readiness for the fifth and final T20I to commence, here at the Warner Park. The umpires are already out to the middle, and now, Mitchell Marsh leads his troops to the field as the Aussies take their fielding positions. Shai Hope and Brandon King are the two openers for West Indies. And the new ball has been handed over to Aaron Hardie, who will begin the proceedings for Australia. King to face. The ump says 'Let's Play Gentlemen' and off we go...

West Indies' Jediah Blades is up for a quick chat with Nikhil Uttamchandani. He begins by saying that he has learnt to stick to the process and execute. He reflects that he tries to pitch the ball in the right areas and get the results. Highlights that he always wanted to play for West Indies and feels it happened quicker than he expected. On playing with his clubmate, Matthew Forde, he tells they share a good camaraderie and they have been good friends since club cricket. Points that his family played a huge role in his success. Mentions that being around some experienced players like Shai Hope and Jason Holder and Alzarri Joseph has helped his confidence a lot.

PITCH REPORT - Daren Ganga is inspecting the deck for this fifth and the final T20I at Basseterre. He first notes the boundary dimensions, pointing out that it is 68 meters down the ground, while the square boundaries are 65 meters and 61 meters. Also shares that this surface is being used for the third time in this series and it's going to offer good rewards for the batters once again. Observes that it is hard and dry with no grass covering. Reckons that the bat will continue to dominate the ball. Also adds that there is an advantage with winning the toss and bowling first due to the small boundary dimensions. He also highlights the importance of planning the bowling order and using angles effectively. He finishes by noting that the home side is playing for pride against a strong Australian team packed with right-handers.

A special occasion for Adam Zampa tonight as he makes his 100th T20I appearance for Australia, becoming the first male Australian bowler to reach the milestone. Ahead of the game, Josh Inglis presents Zampa with a special commemorative cap in the team huddle. Reflecting on the journey that's spanned almost a decade, Zampa shares that T20 cricket has evolved a lot, especially with higher scores and batters striking it cleaner than ever. Admits that he has had to change his style and techniques over the years to keep up with the demands of the format. Mentions that with no red-ball commitments, he has been able to focus entirely on the two white-ball formats. Speaks about the clarity he has always had with his role, especially with the support of coaches and captains he has played under. Zampa modestly admits that he is not the most naturally gifted leg-spinner, and many others have had more mystery or been harder to pick, but doing the small things has helped him succeed at the top level. When asked about the standout moment in his career, Adam says it has to be winning the T20 World Cup in 2021. And when quizzed about whether he has another 10 years left in him, he laughs and responds, 'Definitely not.'

Australia (Playing XI) - Glenn Maxwell, Mitchell Marsh (C), Josh Inglis (WK), Cameron Green, Tim David (In for Cooper Connolly), Mitchell Owen, Aaron Hardie, Ben Dwarshuis (In for Xavier Bartlett), Sean Abbott, Nathan Ellis, Adam Zampa.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Shai Hope (C/WK), Keacy Carty (In for Rovman Powell), Shimron Hetmyer, Sherfane Rutherford, Romario Shepherd, Jason Holder, Matthew Forde, Akeal Hosein, Alzarri Joseph (In for Roston Chase), Jediah Blades.

The skipper of West Indies, Shai Hope says they have just got to try and win this game and make the most of the opportunity to bat first once again. He mentions the importance of learning from the previous games and executing better across all areas. Hope shares that the key lies in playing their best game, and if they do that, he believes they can come out on top. He adds that the guys are raring to go. Informs that Keacy Carty comes in for the injured Rovman Powell and Alzarri Joseph replaces Roston Chase.

The captain of Australia, Mitchell Marsh, says that he hopes for a clean sweep as beating West Indies by 5-0 will be a huge achievement for his side. Also adds that it's another opportunity to represent their nation. Is hopeful they can perform well this time around as well and also tells that everyone wants to be consistent with the process. Notes that the most pleasing thing is their clarity under pressure. On his batting form, he hopes he will get some runs to his name. Also highlights that they maybe 4-0 up, but they have been put under pressure. Informs two changes as Ben Dwarshuis is in for Xavier Bartlett and Tim David comes in for Cooper Connolly.
TOSS - For the FIFTH T20I in a row, the coin has landed in Australia's favour and they have elected to BOWL first.

History beckons for Australia as they eye a clean sweep. A 5-0 win would make them only the second team to achieve this in a T20I series between two Test-playing nations, after India’s feat against New Zealand in 2020. Cameron Green and Josh Inglis have been the torchbearers of the tourists' batting prowess. Adam Zampa, despite being expensive, tops the wicket chart, while Nathan Ellis has stood out with his control. Can the Aussies seal a dominant tour in style? Toss and team news coming up!

It has been a mix of promise and underachievement across the three departments for the West Indies. Shai Hope and Brandon King have been the bright spots with the bat, but despite the firepower in their ranks, the hosts have struggled to finish their innings with a flourish. With the ball, young Jediah Blades, just two T20Is into his career, has emerged as a shining light. However, the attack as a whole has faltered when put under the pump.

Hello, one and all! We are down to the final game of the five-match T20I series. The Aussies have asserted their dominance on this Caribbean sojourn, first in the Tests, and now with a commanding 4-0 lead in the T20Is. They will be eyeing a perfect finish. As for the West Indies, they will be hurting and desperate to salvage some pride with a consolation win.
... MATCH DAY ...

After crushing West Indies 3-0 in the Tests and storming to a 4-0 lead in the T20Is, Australia now chase another clean sweep as the series finale unfolds at Warner Park. Their batting has been ruthless, with Cameron Green anchoring the innings with three fifties in four games, Glenn Maxwell providing explosive starts, and Josh Inglis adding fearless strokeplay in the middle. Mitchell Owen has made a strong impression in his debut series, while Tim David’s blistering 37-ball ton in the third game remains one of the highlights of the tour. The only piece missing is a big knock from skipper Mitchell Marsh, who might just be saving it for the last. With the ball, Adam Zampa has been exceptional as always, supported well by Ben Dwarshuis and Nathan Ellis. The Aussies may also rotate their squad to test bench strength ahead of bigger challenges. For West Indies, Shai Hope and Brandon King have played valuable knocks, but the side needs a more collective effort to compete. Jason Holder and Romario Shepherd’s all-round contributions will be key, while Sherfane Rutherford and Shimron Hetmyer must find consistency in the middle order. Alzarri Joseph remains their pace spearhead, but Akeal Hosein and Gudakesh Motie have a critical role in controlling the scoring rate. The real issue, however, has been defending totals, as they have failed to protect two scores of 200-plus in a row (7 in total, which is the most by any team in this format), which is a worrying sign, but amongst all this, Jediah Blades' spell in the last game was a positive. On a flat Warner Park surface, runs are on offer, but with Australia’s momentum and depth, West Indies will need something extraordinary to avoid a hattrick of whitewashes (minimum of 3 matches played) and salvage some pride.
